title: Why do we divide by \sqrt{dk} in Scaled Dot-Product Attention
prompt: Why do we divide by $\sqrt{d_k}$ in Scaled Dot-Product Attention? Show mathematically that if $Q_i, K_j \sim \mathcal{N}(0, 1)$ independently, their dot product has variance $d_k$, pushing softmax into regions with vanishingly small gradients.
